## Symptom

`_metered_spend()` in `infra/terraform/bedrock-spend-cap/handler.py` accumulates token spend across configured regions, but a single CloudWatch `ClientError` discards totals already collected from healthy regions.

## Confirmed root cause

`_metered_spend()` initializes `total` and `found_series` at lines 280-282, then loops over `REGIONS` at line 283. For each region it creates a CloudWatch client at line 284, lists Bedrock metrics at lines 286-315, and adds priced token values to `total` at lines 332-337. The error handling is all-or-nothing: a listing failure logs and returns `None` at lines 316-318, and a `get_metric_data` failure logs and returns `None` at lines 329-331. There is no per-region degraded state, so a later failed region erases spend already accumulated from earlier healthy regions.

The handler interprets `None` as a full metering outage at lines 507-514. That sets `metered_status = "unavailable"`, may force the effective spend to the threshold, and hides the fact that some regions reported usable token totals.

## Why this matters

The metered value is the fast signal named in the module docstring at lines 17-27. A transient fault in one region should not erase evidence from another region. The current behavior reports less information than the handler has, which makes the state parameter and notifications less accurate during a partial CloudWatch outage.

## Resolved design decision

A partial regional total is a degraded lower bound. It may drive fail-closed attachment when the partial amount reaches the cap, because undercounting can only make that attach later than a full total would. It must not drive release of an existing deny policy, because undercounting could make spend appear below the threshold. Preserve the numeric partial total and carry a degraded/unavailable marker to `handler()` so the release guard at line 562 still sees `signal_unavailable` as true.

Do not treat a partial total as fully available. Do not keep returning bare `None` after a healthy region has contributed spend. If every region fails before any token series contributes, keep the existing unavailable behavior.

## Testing seam

Add the tests to `tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py`. Extend `FakeAWS.client()` from test lines 176-187 so CloudWatch clients can vary by `region_name`, while keeping the existing import seam in `load_handler()` at lines 209-245. The tests should use fake CloudWatch pages and values, not live AWS.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py::test_metered_spend_preserves_partial_total_when_later_region_listing_fails` configures two regions, returns priced tokens from the first region, raises `ClientError` during `list_metrics` in the second region, and observes the first region's dollar total plus a degraded marker under `pytest tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py -k test_metered_spend_preserves_partial_total_when_later_region_listing_fails`.
- [ ] `tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py::test_metered_spend_preserves_partial_total_when_later_region_data_fails` configures two regions, returns priced tokens from the first region, raises `ClientError` during `get_metric_data` in the second region, and observes the first region's dollar total plus a degraded marker under `pytest tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py -k test_metered_spend_preserves_partial_total_when_later_region_data_fails`.
- [ ] `tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py::test_metered_spend_all_regions_fail_reports_unavailable` raises `ClientError` before any region contributes token spend and observes the existing unavailable result under `pytest tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py -k test_metered_spend_all_regions_fail_reports_unavailable`.
- [ ] `tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py::test_degraded_partial_meter_can_attach_but_not_release` proves a degraded partial total at or above `THRESHOLD_USD` attaches the deny policy, while a degraded partial total below `THRESHOLD_USD` leaves an existing deny attached and publishes no release notification under `pytest tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py -k test_degraded_partial_meter_can_attach_but_not_release`.
- [ ] `pytest tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py` exits 0 with the new tests included.
- [ ] `make verify` exits 0.

## Testing

Run `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py -k 'metered_spend_preserves_partial_total_when_later_region_listing_fails or metered_spend_preserves_partial_total_when_later_region_data_fails or metered_spend_all_regions_fail_reports_unavailable or degraded_partial_meter_can_attach_but_not_release'` during development, then run `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" pytest tests/infra/test_bedrock_spend_cap_handler.py`, and finally run `env PATH="$PWD/.venv/bin:$PATH" make verify` before push.

## Source

Raised as an advisory finding by the review bot on Gerrit change 2984 patchset 7 and left out of that change to keep the original fix scoped.
